recap.workouts:
Three pieces, all done.

06:00 Bristlecone plus arms and delts — 78:51 on the file, average heart rate 117, max 170, load 33, RPE 8. That RPE is the honest headline of the morning: Monday was 6, Tuesday 7, yesterday 5, and today — the day written as the smallest on the board — is the hardest rating of the week. Your own log says it before I do: you didn't take the take-it-easy call on the Echo. The EMOM was scaled, which was the right half of the call.

Arms and delts completed every engine target for week 11:
- Triceps pushdown 95 × 15/15/15. TRIGGER FIRED — first full three-set session at 95 and you topped the range on all three. 105 lb is earned, on the lagging muscle you are chasing.
- Barbell curl 60 × 12/10/10. Second session at the bumped 60 with 30 strict pull-ups in front of it, so reps falling was expected and written into the plan. Holds at 60.
- Lateral raise 25 × 10/10/11/11. You took the 25s for all four sets. Ten and eleven reps is five under the range floor — exactly where your own note said a 25 lb debut would land. 20 stays the working load; 25 needs its reps built rather than its load defended.
- Rear delt / face pull 95 × 18, 95 × 15, 90 × 20. Promoted yourself again, 90 to 95, and two of the three sets held inside the range at the new load.

Week 11 hypertrophy now reads Chest 7, Back 7, Side Delts 7, Rear Delts 7, Biceps 7, Triceps 10 — all six targets hit exactly. No muscle short, no muscle padded.

RRe4 — 35:00, 5.10 km, 6:52/km, average heart rate 121, ceiling 131, load 24, RPE 3.

The prescription was 35 minutes of Zone 1 at 5:45–7:17/km. That is precisely what you ran, and then some: every kilometre inside the pace band, and the whole run inside Zone 1 on heart rate too, where Zone 1 runs 121–135 against your run threshold of 167.

km 1 — 6:33/km, average 112
km 2 — 6:34/km, average 116
km 3 — 6:34/km, average 123
km 4 — 7:24/km, average 124 (something took you to walking pace in there)
km 5 — 6:45/km, average 125
last 93 m — average 120

Heart rate climbed for three kilometres and then simply stopped: 123, 124, 125 across the final thirteen minutes at the same effort. Nothing ran away, the ceiling of 131 sits four beats under the top of Zone 1, and the trace carries no fatigue signal anywhere.

Worth the comparison: RRe3 on 12 August, the same recovery slot, ran 6:10/km at an average of 126 with peaks to 146. Today you ran forty seconds per kilometre slower with a fifteen-beat lower ceiling. Same session code, genuinely better restraint.

Bookkeeping: intervals.icu scores the run at 0% compliance and it did not pair. That is not an execution figure — RRe4 was never pushed to the calendar as a planned workout, so there was nothing to compare it against. The morning brief flagged that gap before you ran. The session itself is clean.

And you logged that you felt completely trashed and deeply fatigued, and flagged the run as hard on the phone while the watch put RPE 3 on it. I am not going to argue you out of that. Thirty-five minutes at 121 beats is not a hard enough question to answer it either way.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: RRe4 EXECUTED, and by the numbers it is the best-governed easy run in the block. Every kilometre in the pace band, heart rate flat from kilometre three onward, ceiling 131 against a Zone 1 top of 135. Confidence high — this one is unambiguous. Consequence: proceed. Nothing downstream changes.

2) One honest line about the morning. Thursday's Echo bike calories were named at plan-gen as one of the two non-negotiable scales of the week, and the reason was written down at the time: CrossFit intensity is the budget that funds CMI4. It went at RPE 8, session RPE 630, the largest single number of the week. Not a scolding — you scaled the EMOM, and one firm class does not break a week. But it goes on the ledger, and tomorrow is where it gets paid rather than Saturday.

3) You say you feel deeply fatigued and I am taking that at face value. What stands behind it, without my inventing anything: yesterday was 126 minutes of quality across two sessions, this morning was 79 minutes at your hardest RPE of the week, and your acute load sits at 96 against a chronic 57. That is a real gap, and it is what the last hard stretch of a build week looks like. Tomorrow's session exists precisely for this — which is why it is 60 minutes of pure Zone 1 and nothing else.

4) ADAPT: no-op. Nothing failed and nothing was skipped — the run was executed exactly as written, the class was done firmer than called rather than shorter, and hypertrophy finished the week complete on all six engine targets. So nothing in the remaining week moves: CMI4 stays protected, Sunday's RF12 stays where it is. One trigger banked for Sunday's plan-gen — triceps pushdown 95 → 105, the third triceps step of the block in eleven days. And the standing item, now three days out: the deload conversation is due before Sunday's plan-gen, because Sunday writes the week-12 deload it is about. A gym cap is off the table and is not being re-proposed — the lever is yours to pick.
recap.tomorrow:
Friday, and every part of it is in service of Saturday. 06:00 is pause jerks 6 × 3 at 70–75% on the 2:00 — overhead, light, and they cost the legs nothing. Then Ponderosa, AMRAP 12: take [FITNESS], deadlifts at 155, steady, and stop caring about the round count. A 3-6-9-12 ladder inside twelve minutes is posterior-chain fatigue banked straight against CMI4. No lifting in the same visit — all six engine targets are already complete.

Afternoon is CRe9: 60 minutes of pure Zone 1 at 118–165 W. Not Zone 2, no creep, no lifting it because it feels easy. Last Friday's CRe10 is the benchmark and it is a benchmark for restraint — 75 minutes with a peak of 151 W and zero seconds in Zone 2.

The branch, decided now so nothing has to be improvised. Signals: whether 130 W turns over in the first ten minutes without the effort quietly climbing, whether your heart rate settles under about 135 at those watts, and how the first two rounds of the deadlift ladder feel at 155.

Legs willing? Ride the full 60 minutes of CRe9 anywhere in the Zone 1 band, and take Ponderosa at [FITNESS] exactly as the board writes it. Still flat after ten minutes of spinning? The week plan's own recovery gate answers that one — a rest day beats a recovery spin you drag yourself through — so take the bike off entirely and cruise the class. Both are a good day's work, and CMI4 is protected either way.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

Coach's call, decided on tomorrow morning's numbers rather than tonight's: this is the last item on the week's list and the plan's own designated first full cut. If readiness is still down in the twenties, either drop it outright or ride only the 30' Z2 tail — six Z4 reps is the single biggest block of hard time left in a week whose entire job was to deload. If you wake up genuinely normal, ride it as written and keep the recoveries as lazy as today's were.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.

Everything else about this morning is fine — the snatches are light, the barbell is the lightest of the week, and eight minutes of total work makes this the shortest metcon on the board.

cf.name: Pause Jerk 6×3 @ 70–75% + Ponderosa (AMRAP 12) — [FITNESS] deadlifts, cruise it

On the 2:00 × 6 sets: 3 pause jerks @ 70–75% of 1RM jerk.
Ponderosa — AMRAP 12: [TRAIN] 3-6-9-12… deadlifts 225/155 + 1-2-3-4… wall walks. [FITNESS]: deadlifts 155/105 + inch worm + 2 push-ups.
Call: [FITNESS] deadlifts at 155, steady, and stop caring about the round count. The jerks are fine as written — they are overhead, light, and cost the legs nothing.
An ascending deadlift ladder is the single most CMI4-relevant thing in this week. A 3-6-9-12 ramp inside twelve minutes adds up fast, and it is posterior-chain fatigue banked directly against tomorrow. Friday's entire endurance prescription is a 60′ Zone 1 spin because this exists.

end.name: CRe9 — 60′ pure Zone 1 recovery spin
end.desc:
60′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug — CRe9 is pure Zone 1 despite sitting next to CF10 in the grid row; it is NOT a Zone 2 ride.)
Pure recovery, and today it has a specific job: it is the last thing between you and CMI4.
No Zone 2 creep, no "it felt easy so I lifted it." You have the benchmark and it is a good one: last Friday's CRe10 peaked at 151 W across 75 minutes against a Zone 1 ceiling of 165, with zero seconds in Zone 2 and heart rate moving four beats across the hour. That is the standard, and it is a standard for restraint rather than for output.
This is not the day to find out what your legs have left. Tomorrow is where that question gets asked, and the answer is worth a great deal more then.
If you arrive genuinely flat, a rest day beats a recovery spin you drag yourself through — this is third in the week's cut order, behind the CrossFit intensity and Wednesday's RSP18.

2026-08-22.mind: I have ridden these intervals twice already and I know exactly what they cost, so the only genuinely new thing today is the hour of Zone 1 at the end — and riding that hour honestly, at 140 watts, when I am tired and bored and three hours in, is the actual session.

end.name: CMI4 — THE WEEK'S SESSION (180′)
end.desc:
20′ Z1 → 2 × (20′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W / 15′ Z1) → 10 × (1′ Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 2′ Z1) → 60′ Z1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug — CMI4 is exactly CMI1 plus a 60′ Zone 1 tail; the interval content is identical to both CMI1 and CMI2.)
Nothing about the hard part is new. You have ridden this exact interval content twice: CMI1 in week 9 and CMI2 last Saturday, where block 1 went 224 W, block 2 stepped up to 235 W, and all ten Zone 4 reps held 274 W with peak heart rate flat at 154–158 across the set. The only new thing is the 60-minute Zone 1 tail — double CMI2's.
Target 222–235 W on block 1 and hold it; if heart rate plateaus clearly under 159, block 2 can go a touch firmer, exactly as it did last week. Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step.
On-bike gate for the Zone 4 set: if you cannot get back to Zone 1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set and spin out the remainder. Ending on seven good reps is a completed session; grinding out ten bad ones is not.
The 60′ tail is Zone 1 and only Zone 1 — 118–165 W. It is the entire difference between CMI4 and CMI1, it is where a three-hour ride earns its aerobic keep, and holding 118–165 W for a full hour after two threshold blocks is a genuinely different skill from riding it fresh. Fuel it like the three-hour ride it is.
If Saturday arrives flat, slide this to Sunday and drop RF12. Never water it down into a medium ride. And if the tail specifically is what is in doubt, ride the intervals and shorten the tail — do not trade the tail for firmer intervals.

2026-08-23.mind: Ninety easy minutes the day after three hours on the bike is the hardest restraint the week asks for, and last Sunday I proved I can do it by governing heart rate instead of pace — so I run to a ceiling of 145 again and let the pace be whatever the ground decides.

end.name: RF12 — 90′ long easy run, closes the week and the block
end.desc:
5′ Z1 → 80′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 5′ Z1. (Verified library structure.)
You solved this session last week and the method transfers: govern the heart rate ceiling, not the pace floor. Holding under 145 gave you 90 minutes with a maximum of 149 and zero seconds above Zone 2 by heart rate — the most disciplined long run in your file. Do that again.
Run it off the MIDDLE of the band, around 5:18–5:25/km, not the 5:01 edge. 5:01/km is a wall, not a target. If the ground tips downhill and the pace runs away at an easy heart rate, that is gravity rather than effort — do not go looking for it on purpose, and do not fight it either.
Ninety minutes of honest Zone 2 the day after 180 minutes on the bike is a hard thing to do slowly. Do it slowly — this is the taper of intensity, not of hours.
This is the day the week gives back if Saturday slid. If CMI4 moves to Sunday, this run comes out entirely.
Week 12 is the DELOAD and carries the block's retest — CT31 and RT19.
